plan_review.notes: 3 rounds of adversarial rubber-duck review (gpt-5.4, high reasoning). Round 1 (initial adversarial): rejected, 10 concerns (5 blocking) -> REV2 fixed all 10 with concrete mechanisms (WeakMap arrival observability, progressSuppressed reuse, real-evaluator opportunity preview, BT-computed danger signal, fingerprint anti-retrigger). Round 2 (validation, independently re-read plan.md from disk + repo source): rejected again but narrower -> validated 8/10 original concerns as genuinely resolved, found 2 NEW blocking concerns (one-frame ran:true signal could be missed if update gated behind Progress branch; danger-abort could not guarantee same-tick yield since Progress structurally outranks Engage tree-wide) plus 2 partial residuals (bounded-return-to-combat test claim overclaimed; CLI/env-var plumbing missing) and 1 new non-blocking (settlementAnchor! non-null assertion brittle). Reviewer proposed 3 alternatives (explicit callsite handoff; unconditional-every-poll update; monotonic visit-id/consumed-flag) -> adopted alternative 2 (unconditional pre-tick update, mirroring but stricter than the existing merchantWeaponIntent pre/post-tick split) which resolves both NEW blocking concerns simultaneously -> REV3. Round 3 (narrow validation, scoped only to REV3's 4 remaining items, independently verified every citation against real repo files): 2/4 fully RESOLVED (CLI plumbing; settlementAnchor! removal); 2/4 PARTIALLY RESOLVED with precise mechanical residuals -- (a) arrival-consumption was still ordered after abort checks so a same-frame ran:true could be silently dropped when danger also appeared that frame; (b) danger-interruption test claim overclaimed permanent behavioral identity to a disabled control run when the router's own cooldown/fingerprint design allows future re-arming. Applied both fixes directly (REV4): reordered armed/traveling per-tick checks so arrival-consumption runs unconditionally before any abort check; narrowed the test claim to identical while dangerNearby remains continuously true rather than unbounded. Did not spin a 4th review round since both residuals were narrow, mechanical, reviewer-specified fixes (an ordering swap; a wording precision fix) rather than open design questions -- judged converged. plan_divergence=major_fork because REV3 genuinely re-architected the load-bearing update-timing mechanism (moved from branch-gated update to unconditional pre-tick update) after the reviewer's alternative was adopted over the original design, not merely a detail prune.

rounds.notes: Parallel fan-out: gpt-5.3-codex (code-review agent), gemini-3.1-pro-preview (code-review agent), gpt-5.4 (security-review agent). Security and gemini reviewers returned CLEAN. Codex found 1 Medium finding: the new pre-tick settlement-return hook in bt-ai-provider.ts unconditionally computed findNearestEnemy/getEngageRadius/resolveFloor2SettlementAnchor every poll even when routing is disabled (the default), since updateSettlementReturnIntent itself immediately no-ops when disabled -- wasted per-frame cost on the (default) disabled path. Adjudicated by a dedicated gpt-5.4 (xhigh reasoning) adjudicator agent that read both files directly: VALID + confirmed avoidable. Fix: added isSettlementReturnRoutingEnabled(world) (cheap WeakMap read) to settlement-return-router.ts and gated the entire precompute+call block in bt-ai-provider.ts behind it. Re-verified: typecheck/lint clean, 151/151 targeted tests, 7/7 headless tests, verify:fast green (296 tests). Not yet re-reviewed by a fresh pass at time of round 1 -> proceeded to round 2.

Re-review fan-out after round-1 fix. gpt-5.3-codex confirmed the round-1 perf finding resolved with no new issues (CLEAN). gemini-3.1-pro-preview found 1 new High-severity finding: SETTLEMENT_RETURN_DANGER_COOLDOWN_FRAMES (300) was set SHORTER than SETTLEMENT_RETURN_SERVICE_COOLDOWN_FRAMES (600), directly contradicting its own JSDoc ("longer than the service cooldown so the AI does not immediately re-arm back into the same threat"). Verified via direct file read: discrepancy confirmed exactly as reported. Investigated whether the invariant is load-bearing: the real-time !dangerNearby check in the idle-state transition already gates re-arming against an ACTIVE ongoing threat regardless of cooldown length, so the docstrings specific causal claim is not strictly accurate -- but the documented invariant (danger cooldown > service cooldown) is still a genuine defense-in-depth anti-oscillation buffer consistent with the tasks explicit hysteresis/cooldown requirement, so treated as a valid finding worth fixing rather than silently weakening the requirement or just editing the comment down. Fix: bumped SETTLEMENT_RETURN_DANGER_COOLDOWN_FRAMES to 900 (>600). Grepped all test references first to confirm none hardcode the numeric literal (all use the exported constant symbolically) -- safe change. This fix exposed a latent test-timing issue in the headless happy-path integration test (tests/headless/settlement-return-routing.test.ts): forcing settlement-return eligibility at frame 1 (far from the settlement spawn point) meant every attempt got intercepted by organic Floor2 combat before reaching the settlement, confirmed via a standalone repro script to still never complete a clean cycle even at 30000 frames with the corrected cooldown (not a flaky-luck issue -- fully deterministic and reproducible, so simply raising maxFrames was not a viable fix). Root-caused and fixed by changing the test to seed opportunity right after the mandatory first-visit settlement arrival (mirroring the sibling false-transition-guard test's own documented finding that this seed's AI beelines to the settlement as its first EXPLORE target) instead of at frame 1 -- this starts the return trip from beside the settlement (short, low-risk), which is the realistic "happy path" case; the danger/unreachable interruption paths remain covered in isolation by the dedicated tests elsewhere in the same file. Re-verified: typecheck/lint clean, 151/151 targeted unit/BT/CLI-lib tests, 7/7 headless integration tests (including the previously-failing happy-path test, now passing deterministically), verify:fast green (296 tests). Terminal round (2-round cap) -- clean.
